title: Martin Winterkorn resigns as Volkswagen CEO
trigger: Volkswagen admitted to installing software in diesel vehicles that cheated emissions tests. CEO Martin Winterkorn resigned amid the scandal, known as dieselgate.

timeline.event: US EPA issues notice of violation to Volkswagen for using defeat devices in diesel vehicles
Volkswagen admits 11 million diesel vehicles worldwide contain emissions-cheating software
Martin Winterkorn resigns as CEO of Volkswagen
Matthias Müller named as new CEO of Volkswagen

outcome.summary: Martin Winterkorn resigned as CEO of Volkswagen in September 2015 after the company admitted to installing emissions-cheating software in 11 million diesel vehicles worldwide. The scandal cost Volkswagen billions in fines, buybacks, and legal settlements. Winterkorn was charged by German prosecutors in 2019 but the trial was delayed due to health concerns.

claims.text: US EPA issued a notice of violation to Volkswagen on September 18, 2015 for using defeat devices in diesel vehicles
Volkswagen admitted on September 22, 2015 that 11 million diesel vehicles worldwide contain emissions-cheating software
Martin Winterkorn resigned as CEO of Volkswagen on September 23, 2015
Matthias Müller was named as the new CEO of Volkswagen on September 25, 2015
